title: [D9 Integration] End-to-end fixture run and the acceptance definition
summary: `tests/test_end_to_end.py` runs the six stages over the real wire — the committed ten-record capture published to the pinned broker record by record, consumed back, aggregated by the engine, enriched against a loaded snapshot, rendered, triaged, analysed through a scripted OpenAI-compatible endpoint on the loopback interface, stored as typed rows, emitted, and drained back off the output topic — and asserts exactly the four properties `concept/01-goal-and-scope.md` permits, one test group per claim, all read off the emitted message. `docs/acceptance.md` is the checklist beside it: the four claimable properties with the test that demonstrates each, the eight not-claimable ones, in the note's own three clauses, with the reason, and six things the run does not demonstrate. Three meta-tests keep the note, the checklist and the module from drifting apart, and MNH-20 now requires this file to carry its own disclaimer.
assumption_validated: That 'the prototype works' can be demonstrated by execution at exactly the strength `concept/01` allows, and no further. It can: all four claimable properties hold end to end, over a run that crosses the broker twice and the engine throughout. Building it also produced three findings the prototype did not know about — two contract gaps and one join that overstates coverage — each recorded rather than worked around, which is the result this increment was actually for.
makes_buildable: Task 53 (durability and single-store correctness) and task 55 (deferred register and open-question closure) both get a run they can assert over instead of a stage: `run_pipeline` is one call that produces a `Run` carrying the ingest counters, the projections, the requests, the in-process assessments, the emission counts, the bytes off the topic, every outbound connection Python opened and the structured log, all from one pass. A durability test can take the same harness and restart something in the middle of it. Task 54 (evaluation corpus requirements) gets the not-claimable list already written down with the reason each measurement is blocked, so its job is what a corpus would have to contain rather than what is missing. And any later increment that touches a claim now has a named place to change: adding, removing or rewording a clause in `concept/01`'s claim paragraph is red until `CLAIMS`, `docs/acceptance.md` and a `test_claimN_...` are brought across with it.

verification.detail: 1832 passed in 780 s on the final tree (and 1832 in 721 s on the tree before the last two edits); `uv run pytest -q tests/test_end_to_end.py` alone is 22 passed in 141 s, `-m acceptance` is 33, `-m conformance` is 27 passed in 28 s. `uv lock --check` resolves 17 packages unchanged and `uv run python -m compileall -q src tests scripts` is clean. NO DEPENDENCY WAS ADDED. Every test in the new module executes the whole pipeline against the pinned RisingWave 3.0.3 and the pinned blink 0.2.0: 62 records exist in the sample, 10 are in the committed layer-coverage capture, all 10 crossed the Kafka wire protocol per run and all 10 reconciled against the retained file. SIX GATE MUTATIONS WERE INDUCED, OBSERVED RED AND REVERTED: (1) 'no autonomous remediation occurs' reworded in concept/01 -> test_the_claims_this_module_executes_are_the_notes_own red; (2) a not-claimable clause reworded in docs/acceptance.md -> test_the_checklist_states_the_claims_and_the_ones_it_may_not_make red; (3) the checklist citing a test name that does not exist -> test_the_checklist_names_the_test_that_demonstrates_each_claim red; (4) the second source dropped from the UNION ALL in the test's own migration set -> all three CLAIM-3 tests and the source-outage test red; (5) 'The verdicts are correct.' appended to docs/acceptance.md -> MNH-20 red naming the file and line; (6) the checklist's disclaimer sentence reworded -> MNH-20 red on the missing sentence. The CLAIM-1 enforcement was proved rather than assumed the same way, but as a permanent test: a scripted model citing sixty-four hex characters the rendering never showed produces a typed failure with no verdict and no citations, three attempts deep.
verification.engine_measurements: Measured 2026-09-12 against the running single_node: a migrated schema costs about 190 streaming actors; the engine refuses a new job above `hard limit: 400` per unit of parallelism, so the ceiling on this machine is around 1 600. Three abandoned `helena_test_*` schemas from earlier killed runs were holding 578 of them and made the first full run of this module fail with `MigrationFailed`. Dropping them took the cluster from 851 actors to 273, which is `public` — a deployment schema this session did not touch.

escalations.detail: `RequestVersions.enrichment_snapshot_version` is ONE required identifier and the run found two states it cannot express. (a) A deployment whose only enrichment source has never loaded successfully has no snapshot to name, so it cannot build a request at all — even though the context is perfectly assessable and every entity's status is `failed`, which is exactly the state the pipeline exists to carry through and emit. (b) Two sources with two current snapshots have no single value either. Nothing was invented to get past either: `triage_request` and `snapshot_at` raise `AcceptanceGap` naming the gap, and `test_a_deployment_whose_only_source_is_out_cannot_record_a_snapshot_version` is the refusal executed. This is why CLAIM-2's source-outage case had to be demonstrated with two sources. The snapshot and versioning scheme is still open in `concept/08-open-questions.md`; the fix is a contract decision (a per-source version set, a composite identifier, or an explicit 'no snapshot' value), not a patch.

The enriched-context join asks every source about every entity, including the entity types that source declares it does not cover. `helena.enrichment.SourceDescriptor` refuses a CLAIM outside a source's `entity_types` ('a JA3 list has nothing to say about a domain'); `sql/migrations/0015_enriched_context.sql` takes its source list from the load ledger and LEFT JOINs every entity against it, so ThreatFox — address, domain, url — produces `ok` / `no_match` rows for the six `fingerprint` entities in the committed capture. It does not break the rule `no_match` exists for: the row is a lookup outcome and not a statement of safety. It DOES overstate coverage, and `helena.enrichment.source_diversity` counts over claims, so a future composition rule reading these rows would count a source that could not have consulted anything. Fixing it needs the declared entity types on the SQL side, and 0015's head refuses a second copy of the registry in SQL because a copy can disagree with the decision it copies — so it is a decision. Pinned in both directions by `test_a_source_answers_no_match_about_entity_types_it_declares_it_does_not_cover`.

Adding a source to a RUNNING deployment was not demonstrated and is likely to be a rebuild of the enrichment view chain. `helena_reference_evidence` is a `UNION ALL` created in `sql/migrations/0014`, and a later migration cannot extend it without dropping and recreating everything that reads it — today `helena_analytical_enriched_context` and, through it, the triage-rendering inputs and the sink. What CLAIM-3 demonstrates is the migration set a second source ships as, applied to a fresh schema, which is the honest version of the claim and is what the checklist says.

invariant_conflicts.detail: The task's third step asks for source outages to be 'visible rather than absorbed' end to end, and the smallest reading of that — a single-source deployment whose feed load failed — cannot be run without giving `enrichment_snapshot_version` a value the store does not have. `concept/instruction.md` §2 (every assessment records its versions; replay validates against the version the assessment recorded) and §6 (no silent configuration default) both forbid inventing one, and `docs/decisions/0008-version-registry.md` names a plausible-looking recorded version as the exact thing the registry exists to prevent. The invariant won: the harness raises `AcceptanceGap`, the refusal is a test, and the outage is demonstrated with a second source beside the failed one — which is a real deployment shape and is what the prototype's own catalogue already has two entries for.

The task's first step asks the harness to 'start the broker and engine'. It does not start them itself: `tests/conftest.py` already owns that — it starts a pinned binary when nothing is answering and reuses a running one otherwise, because `single_node` binds fixed meta and compute ports and a second engine cannot run beside the first. A second starter would be a second definition of 'there is an endpoint to ask'. Recorded here rather than silently, because the step names a thing this module deliberately does not do.

deferred: No decision record was added. `docs/acceptance.md` IS the record the task asks for — 'write the acceptance checklist into the repository' — and it carries the reasoning, the findings and the maturity label. A separate ADR restating it would be two documents that can disagree about what may be claimed, which is the one subject where that is least affordable.

The model is scripted and is not the configured endpoint. A run against the live model would measure that model's mood: task 51 recorded a live analyst run returning `schema_invalid` once and validating the next time. The live endpoint is exercised by `tests/test_agents.py`, `tests/test_triage.py` and `tests/test_analyst.py`, which call it; the invalid-response case here is scripted precisely so that the PIPELINE's handling of one is deterministic. Named in the checklist under 'what one run is'.

Truncation is not asserted here. A truncated rendering is visible to the agent and in the request contract, and the output message has no truncation field — the path to a consumer is the agent declaring a `truncated` gap. That truncation is never invisible is MNH-06 in `tests/test_conformance.py`, which is where the property lives; duplicating it would be a second definition. Recorded in the checklist as finding 6.

The CLAIM-4 connection recorder sees Python and not C. `socket.socket.connect` is what it patches, so librdkafka (under `confluent_kafka`) and libpq (under `psycopg`) do not pass through it. That is asserted in BOTH directions — the model endpoint's port is present, the broker's is absent — so the blind spot moving is a failure rather than a silent widening. The two C clients are closed off by `tests/test_dependency_boundary.py`'s equality over the approved distributions and `tests/test_broker.py`'s one-client rule.

No new pytest marker and no new make target. The module joins the existing `acceptance` marker, so `make acceptance` is now the D3 enrichment gate and the D9 run together — which is what an operator asking 'does the prototype do what we say it does' wants, and is 33 tests in under a minute. The Makefile comment and `tests/test_acceptance_enrichment.py`'s docstring were updated to say so rather than left claiming the marker is one module's.

The run is one host, one window, ten records and one snapshot. It is not a load test, a multi-tenant test or a long-window test; what a busy host renders to is `make rendering-size`, which measures it separately. Named in the checklist as finding 4.
lessons: AN END-TO-END RUN IS WHERE A CONTRACT'S MISSING CASE SHOWS UP, AND IT SHOWED UP IMMEDIATELY. Nothing in the package builds an `AgentRequest` from a live context — `assess` is entered with one, and the scheduler that would turn 'every live context' into requests is not part of the first version. So no code had ever had to answer 'which enrichment snapshot does this request record?', and the two states the field cannot express (no source has loaded; two sources have loaded) were both invisible until something had to fill it in from a real store. A stage tested against a hand-built request cannot find this class of gap.

`git checkout <path>` CANNOT RESTORE AN UNTRACKED FILE, AND A MUTATION TEST ON A NEW FILE THEREFORE DOES NOT REVERT ITSELF. Two induced mutations in `docs/acceptance.md` — a new, unadded file — survived their `git checkout`, which failed with `pathspec ... did not match any file(s) known to git` inside a `set -e` block that had already moved on. Both were found and undone by hand. Either `git add -N` the file first, or revert a mutation with the same editor that made it.

A MIGRATED SCHEMA COSTS ~190 STREAMING ACTORS AND AN ABANDONED ONE KEEPS COSTING THEM. RisingWave 3.0.3 refuses a new streaming job above `hard limit: 400` PER UNIT OF PARALLELISM — about 1 600 actors here — and three `helena_test_*` schemas left behind by earlier killed runs were holding 578 of them. The failure arrives as `MigrationFailed` inside whatever test happened to be migrating, which reads like a broken migration and is not one. `docs/runbook.md` §5 has the measurement and the two queries; §10 has the symptom row.

librdkafka AND libpq DO NOT PASS THROUGH `socket.socket.connect`. Patching it records every connection Python opens — `http.client`, `urllib`, a vendored SDK, a raw socket — and none that a C client opens. That makes the patch a good guard for 'did this code call an API it should not have' and a useless one for 'what did this process connect to'. Measured in this run: the model endpoint appears, the broker does not, and the engine would not either.

THE ANALYST MAKES TWO MODEL CALLS PER ESCALATED PASS AND TRIAGE RETRIES THREE TIMES, SO A SHORT SCRIPT IS DIAGNOSED AS THE WRONG FAILURE. A scripted endpoint that runs out of answers hands the next agent the previous agent's answer, and the run ends as `schema_invalid` complaining that `malicious.c2` is not a triage root — which looks like a contract bug and is a script that was one entry short. Script triage's retries and the analyst's two calls explicitly, and let the endpoint's own 'called more times than scripted' assertion be the thing that fires.

A CITATION CANNOT BE WRITTEN BEFORE THE RUN. An `evidence_id` is a sha256 over the claim, the snapshot and the identity, so a scripted model answer that cites one has to be built AFTER the rendering exists. Making the script a callable over the requests rather than a list is what makes that possible, and it is also what turns the model's answer into an input to the run instead of a source of flakiness in it.
failed_approaches: Demonstrating a source outage end to end with ONE source. It cannot be done without inventing a version: `failed` requires that no snapshot covers the window, which is the same condition as having no `enrichment_snapshot_version` to record. Three arrangements were considered and rejected before anything was written — a failed attempt after a successful load (the earlier snapshot stays valid, so the status is `ok`/`stale`, which is the loader's documented behaviour and correct), a successful load dated after the window (its validity does not cover the window either, so the status is `missing` and there is still no version), and a sentinel value (a recorded version naming no snapshot, which is precisely what `docs/decisions/0008` exists to prevent). The second source is the arrangement that works and it is a real deployment shape.

A citation to a completed negative. `no_match` rows carry no `evidence_id` — they are the LEFT JOIN finding nothing to join, so there is no stored row to identify — so a test that asserted every emitted evidence row has an identifier fails, and an agent cannot cite 'nobody has heard of this'. CLAIM-1 is about the positives, and the module says so where it would otherwise look like an omission.

Asserting that the fingerprint entities carry no evidence at all — the 'nobody to ask' sixth case of `sql/migrations/0019_sink.sql`. They carry `threatfox` / `ok` / `no_match` instead, because the join does not read a source's declared entity types. That is the second escalation above; the assertion was replaced by a test that pins the actual behaviour and names it as a finding.
next_session_should_know: The acceptance definition exists, it is executable, and it found three things on the way in. SEVEN THINGS TO CARRY. (1) `docs/acceptance.md` IS THE ANSWER TO 'DOES THE PROTOTYPE WORK', AND IT IS ENFORCED FROM THREE SIDES. `tests/test_end_to_end.py` parses `concept/01-goal-and-scope.md`'s claim paragraph on every run and holds `CLAIMS` to it verbatim; it requires a `test_claimN_...` per claim and resolves every test the checklist cites; and MNH-20 in `tests/test_conformance.py` requires the checklist's own disclaimer sentence and scans it for accuracy claims with every other markdown file. Adding, removing or rewording a claim is red in all three until the change is carried across. All six of those failure modes were induced and reverted. (2) `run_pipeline` IS THE HARNESS AND IT IS ONE CALL. It takes a connection, a bootstrap, a temp path, a model script and a feed plan, and returns a `Run` holding the ingest counters, the projections, the requests, the assessments, the emission counts, the messages off the topic, the outbound connections and the log. Use it rather than wiring the stages again; a scenario is a `FeedPlan` and a script, which is how stale, failed, invalid-response and two-source runs are all built. (3) THE HARNESS REFUSES RATHER THAN PICKS, AND BOTH REFUSALS ARE FINDINGS. `snapshot_at` raises `AcceptanceGap` when two sources hold a snapshot valid at the window, and `triage_request` raises when none does. `RequestVersions.enrichment_snapshot_version` is one identifier and those are the two states it cannot express — see the escalations. If a later increment needs a request for such a context, that is the contract decision to take to the operator, not a value to fill in. (4) THE ENRICHMENT JOIN ASKS EVERY SOURCE ABOUT EVERY ENTITY. ThreatFox answers `no_match` about JA3 fingerprints it declares it does not cover. It is not a safety claim and nothing reads it as one, but it overstates coverage and `source_diversity` would count it. `test_a_source_answers_no_match_about_entity_types_it_declares_it_does_not_cover` pins it; fixing it means the declared entity types on the SQL side, which 0015's head argues against. (5) `make acceptance` IS NOW TWO MODULES. The D3 enrichment-state gate and the D9 run, 33 tests, under a minute, both part of `make test`. The Makefile comment and `tests/test_acceptance_enrichment.py`'s docstring say so; do not re-narrow either to one module. (6) ABANDONED TEST SCHEMAS BREAK THE NEXT MIGRATION. ~190 actors each, ceiling ~1 600, and a killed run cannot drop its own. If a test fails with `MigrationFailed ... the number of actors exceeds the limit`, it is not the migration — `docs/runbook.md` §5's last block has the two queries and §10 has the symptom row. Drop only `helena_test_*` and `helena_e2e_*`; `public` is a deployment's store. (7) THE MODEL IN THIS RUN IS SCRIPTED ON PURPOSE, AND THE SCRIPT IS A CALLABLE OVER THE REQUESTS because a citation names an identifier that does not exist until the run has happened. Triage retries three times and the analyst asks twice per escalated pass; a script one entry short is diagnosed as a contract bug rather than as a short script.
